description: Adds two lifecycle trends so Sparkline's x-coordinate ternary in src/components/MetricsDashboard/index.js renders both of the arms the real data does not reach, in the one ordinary coverage build. `coverageFixture` carries exactly one value and takes the `values.length === 1 ? 50` arm, which centres a lone point because the expression beside it divides by `values.length - 1`. `coverageFixtureEmpty` carries no values and returns "No trend data yet" before the ternary is reached. The checked-in data defines two real trends, `submissions` and `publications`. `submissions` was empty while no open reference-architecture submissions were observed, and supplied the no-values arm for free; it fills in as soon as a collector run records open submissions, so that arm cannot be left to it. A trend holding one point, and a trend holding none, are both ordinary shapes -- a collector run that reaches a source with nothing to report emits the trend with an empty `values`. These are `add` rather than `append` or `set` onto a real trend on purpose: patching a real trend would trade the arm it already renders for the one under test rather than add a case, which is why these arms previously needed the variant build. Adding trends beside the real ones is additive in the sense tests/e2e/data-fixtures.spec.js means -- both real trends keep rendering exactly as they did -- so all three Sparkline arms render on the one real /resources/metrics page in one build, and the variant overlay is freed to clear `referenceArchitectureLifecycle.trends` outright for LifecycleSection's `|| {}` trends fallback. Each key must be absent from the real data or the build fails, so a collector run that grows a trend of either name breaks here instead of having it silently overwritten.

referenceArchitectureLifecycle.trends.co.label: Coverage fixture trend with a single point
Coverage fixture trend with no points
